newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on Plains rainfall.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on Plains rainfall.

text.p: Rainfall this week in some key hard red winter wheat areas of the U.S. Great Plains pressured CBOT soft red winter wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
"They had good rains in the Southwest, China's crop is looking good and seasonally wheat should be going down anyway," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.

Cash sources said beneficial rain fell this week in panhandles of Texas and Oklahoma and in southwest Kansas. These wheat growing areas were in need of rain and the moisture will help boost crop prospects, cash dealers said.
Overall good crop conditions in the U.S. soft red winter wheat region also continued to weigh on the market, sources said.
Technicians said the wheat market broke this week on fund long liquidation. Sell-stops of up to 10 million bushels were hit in late and fast dealings Thursday, they said.
Bearishness from a sharp, nearly limit-down move in soybean futures also spilled into the wheat market.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 11 cents per bushel lower, with May down 3-1/4 at $3.71-3/4 a bushel. July closed down 1-1/2 cents at $3.71-1/2.

There was late talk China may be seeking wheat and there may have been some underpinning on news India's state-run State Trading Corp (STC) said Friday it had contracted to import 2.74 million tonnes of wheat since December 1996, floor sources said.

"We have firmed up (import) contracts for a total of 2.74 million tonnes of wheat (since December 1996)," STC chairman B.K. Chaturvedi told reporters. He said STC contracted to import 1.74 million tonnes in 1996-97 (April-March).
"We have firmed up contracts for one million tonnes more. This was done in the last week of March," Chaturvedi said.

Technicians said first support in the May was at $3.69-1/2 and second support was at $3.54-1/2. The session low for May was $3.68. First resistance was at $3.84-1/2 and second resistance was at $3.99-1/2. The session high for May was $3.74.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 42 percent. The market generally views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
FIMAT Futures was a key bear spreader of 2.5 million bushels of July/May at 1-1/2 to two cents per bushel, premium July, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services spread one million bushels of May/July at 1-1/2 to two cents, premium July, traders said.
Dean Witter and Refco Inc each sold three million bushels of July, traders said. Refco Inc also bought two million bushels of July, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 28,000 contracts, above the 26,000 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 500 May $4.00 puts at 31 cents and sold 500 July $3.70 puts at 20 cents, traders said. FIMAT also bought 500 May $3.90 puts at 21 cents and sold 500 July $3.60 puts at 14 cents, they said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, above the 6,319 traded Thursday.
